top_story.headline: Raskin Bill Would Put Trump-Era "Propaganda, Corruption and Authoritarianism" on Permanent Smithsonian Display
top_story.dek: The House held a two-minute session Tuesday with no votes, but 22 measures were introduced.
paragraphs: With no votes and no debate, the most pointed measure introduced on Tuesday, October 6, was H.R. 10765 from Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD-8). It would direct the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution to collect, preserve and display in a permanent exhibition at the National Museum of American History artifacts reflecting "the rise of governmental propaganda, corruption, and authoritarianism" during Donald J. Trump's two presidencies, covering January 20, 2017 through January 20, 2021 and January 20, 2025 through January 20, 2029.

The bill was referred to the Committee on House Administration and, for a period to be determined by the Speaker, the Committee on Natural Resources. The bill text as printed in the Congressional Record lists no cosponsors.

Also introduced was H.R. 10764 by Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI-4), the Executive Settlement Review Act, which would require certain procedures for compromise settlements or awards for executive branch officials.

sections.headline: House meets for two minutes; 22 bills and resolutions introduced
paragraphs: The Senate met in pro forma session for 33 seconds on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, and adjourned until 1:30 p.m. on Friday, October 9. The House met at 4 p.m. and adjourned at 4:02 p.m.; the Daily Digest records no Yea and Nay votes, no recorded votes and no quorum calls.

Even so, the House received 17 public bills (H.R. 10751–10767), one concurrent resolution and four simple resolutions. The newsworthy ones: Raskin's Smithsonian exhibition bill, Rep. Josh Gottheimer's resolution marking the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 attacks on Israel (H.Res. 1618, with a long cosponsor list), and Rep. John James's tariff-funded relief program. Two committee reports were also filed: H.R. 6698 and H.R. 7260, both on veterans' matters. The full list follows.

items: H.R. 10751, sponsored by Rep. Jack Bergman (R-MI-1) — would remove restrictions on dental therapist services under the Community Health Aide Program of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources and the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10752, sponsored by Rep. Troy A. Carter (D-LA-2) — would create a task force on artificial intelligence inside the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency; referred to the Committee on Homeland Security.

H.R. 10753, sponsored by Rep. Elijah Crane (R-AZ-2) — the Tribal Veterans Voucher Flexibility Act, which would let the Tribal HUD-VASH housing voucher program reallocate vouchers on a voluntary basis; referred to the Committee on Financial Services.

H.R. 10754, sponsored by Rep. Elijah Crane (R-AZ-2) — the Rural Disaster Fairness Act of 2026, which would update indicators of the local impact of a disaster in the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018; referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

H.R. 10755, sponsored by Rep. Jasmine Crockett (D-TX-30) — would name the Cedar Hill, Texas, post office at 475 East FM 1382 the "Eugene Gates Jr. Post Office Building"; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
H.R. 10756, sponsored by Rep. Mike Ezell (R-MS-4) — would reauthorize Regional Ocean Partnerships; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.
H.R. 10757, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — would limit U.S. contributions to the United Nations; referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.R. 10758, sponsored by Rep. Jeff Hurd (R-CO-3) — would have the Secretary of Veterans Affairs award grants to state entities to expand structured outdoor recreation programs for veterans; referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

H.R. 10759, sponsored by Rep. John James (R-MI-10) — would set up a tariff-funded program to protect U.S. manufacturers, workers, farmers and supply chains from economic harm caused by tariffs and foreign retaliation, and to encourage reshoring; referred to the Committee on Financial Services and the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10760, sponsored by Rep. Thomas H. Kean Jr. (R-NJ-7) — would create a multiagency Middle School Mental Health Task Force at the Department of Education and the Department of Health and Human Services; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10761, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) — the Campus Accountability and Safety Act of 2026, which would amend the Jeanne Clery Campus Safety Act to combat campus sexual assault; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10762, sponsored by Rep. Michael Lawler (R-NY-17) — the Anthony Amoros Law Right to Know Act, which would require used-vehicle sellers to maintain a functional airbag system or clearly disclose when one is missing or disabled; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10763, sponsored by Rep. Julia Letlow (R-LA-5) — the Know Your Risk Act, which would direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to report to Congress on breast cancer risk assessment tools; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10764, sponsored by Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI-4) — the Executive Settlement Review Act, which would amend title 31 of the U.S. Code to require certain procedures for compromise settlements or awards for executive branch officials; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10765, sponsored by Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD-8) — would direct the Smithsonian Institution to collect, preserve and display, in a permanent exhibition at the National Museum of American History, artifacts reflecting the rise of governmental propaganda, corruption and authoritarianism during the two presidencies of Donald J. Trump; referred to the Committee on House Administration and the Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10766, sponsored by Rep. Keith Self (R-TX-3) — would direct the Secretary of Defense to add assets critical to the Golden Dome missile defense system to the Department of Defense Critical Asset List; referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10767, sponsored by Rep. Adrian Smith (R-NE-3) — the Fair Play Enforcement Act, which would impose an excise tax on colleges and universities that allow specified individuals to take part in intercollegiate athletics; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H. Con. Res. 123, sponsored by Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez (D-NM-3) — would recognize the wage disparity faced by Latinas and its effect on women, families and the economy; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.

H.Res. 1617, sponsored by Rep. Earl L. "Buddy" Carter (R-GA-1) — would recognize October as "American Pharmacy Month" in honor of pharmacists and pharmacy teams; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.Res. 1618, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — would mark the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023, terrorist attacks on Israel, honor the victims and hostages, and call for the complete disarmament of Hamas; it lists a long roster of cosponsors; referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.
H.Res. 1619, sponsored by Rep. Glenn Thompson (R-PA-15) — would reaffirm German-American friendship and support continued U.S.-Germany cooperation; referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.Res. 1620, sponsored by Rep. Nikema Williams (D-GA-5) — would support the goals and ideals of "National Nonviolence Week" to raise awareness of youth violence; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
